title: Category Theory
text:
1.1 Introduction

1.1.1 Natural transformation

Let \(f \in L^1(X\times Y)\). Then \[ \int_X\!\int_Y f(x,y)\,dy\,dx = \int_Y\!\int_X f(x,y)\,dx\,dy. \]


Definition 1 A group is a set \(G\) with a binary operation \(\cdot\) satisfying: 1. Associativity: \((a\cdot b)\cdot c=a\cdot(b\cdot c)\); 2. Identity: \(\exists e\in G\) such that \(e\cdot a=a\cdot e=a\); 3. Inverses: \(\forall a\in G\ \exists a^{-1}\in G\) such that \(a\cdot a^{-1}=a^{-1}\cdot a=e\).


The set \(\mathbb Z\) with addition is a group.


Lemma 1 The product of two integers is even if at least one factor is even.


Theorem 1 There are infinitely many prime numbers.


Proof. Assume finitely many primes \(p_1,\dots,p_n\).
Consider \(P=p_1\cdots p_n+1\).
\(P>1\) has a prime divisor \(p\), but \(p\) divides neither \(P-1\) nor \(1\), contradiction.


Corollary 1 For every integer \(n\ge 2\) there exists a prime \(p>n\).


Remark 1. Euclid’s proof is constructive: it gives an upper bound on the next prime.

title: Extemporaneous Reconstruction by Subjects
text: We present an on-the-fly reconstruction framework in which subjects spontaneously regenerate missing or corrupted information. Preliminary results indicate high inter-rater reliability and robust generalization across domains.

title: Extemporaneous Reconstruction by Subjects
text:
1. Introduction
Traditional pipelines require pre-computed templates. Here, subjects reconstruct stimuli extemporaneously, yielding richer and more adaptable outputs.

title: Extemporaneous Reconstruction by Subjects
text:
2. Methods

Participants: 64 undergraduate volunteers.

Materials: 120 semi-structured prompts.

Procedure: Subjects spoke for 90 s per prompt; audio was transcribed and coded in real time.

title: Extemporaneous Reconstruction by Subjects
text:
3. Results
Mean reconstruction accuracy = 87.3 % (SD = 8.1). Figure 1 shows the distribution of scores.
